residual_risks: The adaptive CE wrappers, top-level fused-MLP autograd path and direct ownership call graph have not compiled or executed in the target torch-neuronx/NKI environment; Python movement can change graph capture or compilation despite identical arithmetic/kernel ASTs.
Local CPU verification used a non-target PyTorch build. It cannot establish Neuron numerical equivalence, NKI grid behavior, four-rank device collectives, compile time, step rate or memory pressure.

The explicit ownership design deliberately splits APIs: the base optimizer owns param_groups and zero_grad while OwnedOptimizer owns distributed step and ownership-aware state. Current main and checkpoint behavior are correct, but future resume code must call the owner state API rather than the raw base optimizer state API.
The builder's assert-based fail-closed checks are disabled by python -O; use the normal interpreter and verify generated hashes, as done here.

The proposal says fresh BPB must remain within predeclared run-to-run noise but does not state a numeric BPB band. A supervisor/analyst must define or explicitly resolve that acceptance criterion before calling the hardware result a quality pass.
Automated reviewer acceptance and private-shard BPB cannot be guaranteed by these local checks.
